question: Which is the smallest bone in the human body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Stapes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stapes**__

 __
 
• The **smallest bone in the human body** is called **stapes**, located in the **middle ear**.
 
• The size of the staples is 3mm x 2.5mm.
 
• There are three bones in the middle ear, Malleus, Stapes, and Incus.
 
• The Stapes is the smallest of the three bones and it looks like a bell.
 
• It is the innermost bone of our auditory ossicles in the middle ear, which are responsible for transmitting sound waves from the air outside to the fluid-filled labyrinth (cochlea).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phalanges**__

 __
 
• The phalanges are the bones that make up the fingers of the hand and the toes of the foot.
 
• There are 56 phalanges in the human body, with fourteen on each hand and foot.
 
 
 
• **Humerus**__
 __
 
• The humerus is a long bone in the arm that runs from the shoulder to the elbow.
 
• It connects the scapula and the two bones of the lower arm.
 
 
 
• **Pelvis**__
 
 
• The Pelvis is the lower part of the trunk, between the abdomen and the thighs together with its embedded skeleton.
